transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Oakcrest CTO), Daniel (ML Eng), Lena (Infra), Priya (Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to understand Oakcrest's model selection constraints — they run a multilingual customer insights product, need long-context for conversation history (20k+ tokens), tool-calling to query internal DBs and a search index, and a preference for private deployment or VPC-hosted control plane due to PII. Interested in cost/latency tradeoffs and comparison between quantized open models vs hosted proprietary APIs.

Topics:
- context length needs and typical session shapes
- multilingual & code-switching support (EN/ES/FR + mix)
- tool-calling/function-calls for DB + retrieval + actions
- deployment choices: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
- performance benchmarking and pilot plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick 30 minute scoping then leave time for q and a, i'm Samira from Redwood, this is Ethan our SE.
[00:10] Maya: thanks, yeah thanks Samira. Quick context — Oakcrest builds a multilingual insights assistant that ingests support chats and returns summarized action items. We have a lot of PII; so isolation and auditability are mandatory.
[00:24] Ethan: great, can you say more about your typical convo length? is this mostly short tickets or long threads?
[00:31] Daniel: it's pretty variable. average is like 3–5 messages but we want to support threaded histories up to 18k tokens — sometimes 25k when you include attachments text. The model needs to keep persona context + previous resolutions.
[00:44] Lena: and latency we care about — p95 sub 600ms for single-turn, but for long context we can tolerate 1.5s for generation, as long as throughput is okay for batch analytics jobs.
[00:56] Samira: ok, got it. so main asks: large context support, multilingual competency, tool-calling into your search index and our internal DBs, and security posture. on deployment are you leaning private or hosted?
[01:10] Priya: product would prefer hosted for faster iteration but security's pushing for VPC or private because of retention rules — we might do a pilot hosted with token redaction then shift to dedicated or private.
[01:21] Maya: yes security is the blocker. we also have EU data residency needs for some customers.
[01:26] Ethan: under Redwood we have three modes — hosted API (fastest to get started), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation), Private (VPC / on prem with control plane options). Dedicated can be VPC peered for tighter network controls.
[01:40] Daniel: what's the practical context limits? like you listed 32k on the site — is that for all models?
[01:44] Ethan: good question. context limits are model dependent — some open models we host/optimize up to 32k with kv cache optimizations, others are 8k or 16k. we also offer prefix caching to keep conversation vectors hot so effectively you can stitch longer histories with retrieval. but yes, if you need native 25k windows we should pick model variants that support that or do dynamic retrieval.
[02:00] Maya: is the 32k work with quantized models? our cost team loves quant but worried about accuracy drift for summarization.
[02:08] Ethan: quantization often reduces size but can affect subtle hallucination patterns — our Optimize team suggests mixed strategy: use a quantized 8-bit variant for bulk tasks and a higher-precision model for final summarization/critical outputs. we can show benchmarks.
[02:20] Priya: when you say model variants which models are you recommending for multilingual + long context?
[02:25] Samira: typically we'd evaluate a couple: a performant open-native long-context model (e.g., LlamaX long-context variant), a Mistral/Falcon-family for throughput, and a heavier foundation model for quality when needed. names can vary and the transcription might for sure flip names — but we'll provide a curated shortlist and perf matrix.
[02:40] Daniel: do you support tool-calling? we want to call our internal action API and a vector search endpoint.
[02:46] Ethan: yes — Redwood supports structured tool-calling / function calling; we can orchestrate calls to your retrieval layer, execute safe side-effect functions with RBAC, and log all calls in audit logs. for Private setups we can keep keys in customer KMS/HSM.
[02:59] Lena: about keys and encryption — KMS integration, hardware module, is that available in Dedicated?
[03:04] Ethan: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via VPC peering and can use customer HSM for signing. Private deployment gives the most control including on-prem HSMs.
[03:13] Maya: any blockers with our on-prem data pattern — we process scanned docs with OCR, sensitive fields need to be redacted before leaving their environment.
[03:20] Samira: right — we have a couple of approaches: you can do client-side redaction/tokenization, or keep the model in a private footprint and only surface metadata. for pilots we'll often run hosted with redaction layer in front, then move to Dedicated/VPC once the flow is validated.
[03:35] Daniel: curious about throughput — we expect ~500 qps for embeddings and 200 qps for generation during peak. is dedicated the right fit?
[03:42] Ethan: that's a medium-to-large footprint. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can configure autoscale/queues. we'd size GPU pools based on your prompt distribution; we'll propose an initial capacity plan in the benchmark doc.
[03:54] Priya: ok and multilingual quality — how do you test? we need Spanish + French + code-switching for LatAm customers.
[04:02] Ethan: we run evals with curated prompt sets per language and domain. we'll request sample transcripts from you to include in the benchmark. quality varies by model family; some models have better low-resource language support.
[04:14] Maya: another concern: vendor lock-in. if we start on hosted and later want to run on-prem, what's migration look like?
[04:20] Samira: migration is by design — same API surface and config across modes. you can pin model versions, export prompt templates and evaluation results. full on-prem requires more infra but we help with packaging and a migration plan.
[04:33] Daniel: what about tooling — how are function calls authored? is it OpenAI-like function calling or something proprietary?
[04:39] Ethan: we support OpenAI-style function schemas plus a Redwood tool manifest that can be deployed per-tenant. it's flexible so your engineers can define types and safe-guards.
[04:50] Maya: any compliance paperwork we should expect? SOC2 yes, do you have certs and are audit logs retained for how long?
[04:57] Samira: we maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts, can provide audit attestation. log retention is configurable — default for hosted is 90 days; Dedicated/Private you control retention, and we can support longer retention for an add-on.
[05:09] Lena: would Dedicated give us the ability to keep logs inside our VPC?
[05:12] Ethan: yes, with VPC peering you can push logs to your S3 or logging endpoint; Private gives full control.
[05:20] Priya: cost question — what's the delta between quantized open models and hosted proprietary price?
[05:25] Samira: rough rule of thumb: quantized open models on Dedicated can be 2–6x cheaper per token vs managed proprietary hosted APIs depending on size and batching. we'll put exact numbers in a comparison spreadsheet tailored to your expected session shapes.
[05:38] Daniel: bench plan — what do you need from us to run an apples-to-apples eval?
[05:43] Ethan: sample transcripts across languages, expected prompt/response distributions, a few representative tool-call schemas, and a set of success metrics (latency p95, summary quality scores, hallucination tolerance). we'll run token-level cost sims and small perf runs.
[05:58] Maya: timeline — we'd like a pilot in 4 weeks, starting with hosted trial plus privacy redaction to prove concept. if that goes well, move to Dedicated in quarter.
[06:07] Samira: sounds feasible. next steps: we will send the cost comparison and SOC2 docs today, Ethan will propose a benchmark plan and a 2-hour deep-dive window for next week.
[06:16] Priya: thanks, can you also include routing options? we might want to route EU requests to EU region and fall back to a cheaper variant.
[06:23] Ethan: yes, smart routing by region/cost/latency is available — we'll document policies and a simple fallback plan.
[06:30] Maya: a few micro-questions — (1) do you support streaming partial generations for UX? (2) can we pin models per route? (3) how do you handle KV cache across restarts?
[06:40] Ethan: (1) yes streaming; (2) yes pin per-route; (3) KV cache can be checkpointed and we have options for cold-start policies and prefix caching to reduce warm-up overhead.
[06:51] Daniel: any gotchas with long-context and tool-calling — mixing retrieval with long context sometimes confuses the model.
[06:57] Ethan: totally — we recommend retrieval-augmented prompts where the retrieval results are structured and tool calls use clear schemas; we'll include prompt templates and a debugging checklist.
[07:07] Maya: ok great.
[07:09] Samira: recap — Samira to send pricing/compliance docs, Ethan to send bench plan and available slots for deep dive, Oakcrest to share sample data and redaction rules. we'll target a pilot within ~4 weeks.
[07:21] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
